newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money eases on reduced demand, gilts up.
newsitem.headline: India call money eases on reduced demand, gilts up.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday in the 7.5-8.0 percent range, down from the opening 10.75-11.0 percent, on poor demand for funds, dealers said.
They said rates came down as most banks had already covered their positions ahead of the reporting day. Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.
"There was little pressure on rates today," said a dealer. "Lenders were trying to push up rates, but there were no takers at higher levels."

He said call rates were likely to settle down in a seven to eight percent range next fortnight as additional liquidity would be infused through a cut on January 4 in banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 10.5 percent from 11 percent.
Dealers said prices of government securities were firm in brisk trade with good demand seen for securities with maturities up to 1999.
"Some banks are taking up positions ahead of Saturday's CRR cut," a dealer said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock firmed up to 102.90 rupees on Thursday from its last traded 102.74, dealers said.

The 12.00 percent 1999 stock gained to 98.75 rupees from 98.37 while the 13.65 percent 1999 hardened to 102.75 rupees from 102.0, they said. In longer-dated securities, the 12.50 percent 2004 rose to 95.49 rupees from 94.85, they said.
